title: Zero-downtime log schema migrations and incremental index coordinator
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Background: Our structured log ingestion pipeline needs to evolve schema fields (new request.path_category, user.session_id) without downtime or expensive re-ingests. Current index mappings in Loki/ELK are brittle: schema changes cause index rebuilds, query regressions, and gap windows for searches.

Goal: Implement a zero-downtime migration pattern and a coordinator service that applies incremental index updates, maintains a live compatibility layer, and backfills only the minimal materialized fields. The coordinator will orchestrate: (1) schema flags published in the ingestion layer, (2) dual-write mode for new fields, and (3) staged index mapping updates with canary query verification.

Technical approach:
- Schema flagging: add a schema_version header to every log envelope emitted by edge/sidecars. Ingest gateway will tag events and route to migration-aware adapters.
- Dual-write path: ingestion adapters will start writing new fields into a parallel lightweight index alias (index_v2) while continuing to populate primary index (index_v1).
- Incremental index coordinator: a small stateful service (index-coordinator) tracks migration state per log-stream (per-app) and performs: mapping updates, alias swaps, and controlled backfills (windowed, rate-limited).
- Canary verification: coordinator runs query-level checks against index_v2 for a rolling subset of tenants and compares result parity/latency with index_v1 before promoting.
- Backfill strategy: use a streaming backfill job that replays compressed raw log blobs, extracts only new fields and writes them to index_v2. Backfill will be throttled and checkpointed to avoid I/O storms.
- Rollback: alias-level swap back to index_v1 and mark schema_version as aborted; coordinator triggers garbage-collection of index_v2 after a safe window.

Acceptance criteria:
- No ingestion downtime during schema rollout (0% traffic interruption).
- Query parity >= 99.5% on canary tenants for 24h after promotion.
- Controlled backfill can sustain <= 10% additional I/O on store cluster.
- Migration coordinator exposes metrics: migrations_in_progress, canary_pass_rate, backfill_lag_seconds, promoted_count.

Observability and safety: Add dashboards (migration-runbook, per-stream health), tracing spans for coordinator operations, and SLO alerts on promotion parity and backfill lag. Include automated abort if parity < 98% after two retries.
acceptance_criteria: No ingestion downtime for production traffic during migration
Canary parity >= 99.5% for 24h before full promotion
Backfill does not exceed configured I/O budget (default 10%)
Coordinator exposes metrics and traces used by runbooks
Rollback path tested end-to-end in staging
implementation_notes: Will add schema_version header in sidecar v2.1 (sidecar PR: github.com/redwood-inference/sidecar/pull/182)
Index-coordinator will be written in Go and deployed as a small stateful replica set behind leader-election
Use existing aliasing primitives in Elasticsearch and label-based index routing in Loki
Backfill will reuse the ingest-replay worker with a new extraction plugin to limit memory pressure
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Backfill spikes store I/O -> Mitigation: rate-limited streaming backfill with token bucket and circuit breaker
Risk: Query semantics diverge due to data normalization -> Mitigation: canary parity checks and sample-based diffing tool (see github PR)
Risk: Coordinator state loss -> Mitigation: durable checkpoints in etcd and safe-mode failover path

2025-02-20 - Oliver Chen: Prototype index-coordinator leader election and alias swap flow. Local e2e against a single ES node passed. Draft PR posted: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/241 — need infra review for persistent storage path.
2025-02-24 - Design review (Ana Ruiz): Suggested adding metric for backfill_bytes_written and an automated stop condition when store latency exceeds threshold. Added to acceptance criteria.
2025-02-27 - QA (Devon Brooks): Runbook draft available in Confluence. Will run full migration simulation in staging using 7 days of compressed logs (snapshot id: staging-snap-20250225).

2025-03-01 - Oliver Chen: Canary run started for app-team alpha. Observed 99.7% parity at 6h, promotion scheduled for 2025-03-03 pending 24h stability window. Backfill initial pass completed for 3 days of history with 6% I/O overhead.
Next steps: finish sidecar rollout to ingestion fleet, finalize infra permissions for coordinator, and schedule full staging dry-run week of 2025-03-08.
review_feedback: Security: ensure schema_version header cannot be set by untrusted client (validated in gateway).
Observability: add tracing span for backfill-window-start and backfill-window-finish to tie to stored metrics.
SRE: recommend a canary tag system per-app to limit blast radius; coordinator should support partial promotions
